title: Movie ticket booking
scopeHtml: Scope: Seat locking with TTL, double-booking prevention, atomic multi-seat holds. Questions are still to be written.

notes.title: Requirements
notes.html:
Design a movie ticket booking system (BookMyShow style): browse shows, pick seats, hold them while paying, confirm the booking, and never sell one seat twice.

Clarify: one theatre or many? Seat map per show? How long is a hold (typically 5 to 10 minutes)? Can a user book several seats at once (yes, all-or-nothing)? Payment is external and can fail or time out. Pricing tiers and cancellation are follow-ups. (Here: shows with a seat grid, atomic multi-seat hold with TTL, confirm after payment, release on failure.)

Worked example. A show has 50 seats (5 rows x 10). Alice holds A1,A2 at 10:00 with a 5-minute TTL (expiry 10:05). Bob tries A2,A3 at 10:01: A2 is locked so he gets nothing, and A3 must stay free (atomicity). Bob retries for A3 only and gets it. Alice pays at 10:03 and A1,A2 become BOOKED. On Friday night with 3,000 users on one blockbuster show, many will click the same "best seats" at the same second; exactly one may win each.

Industry examples. BookMyShow, PVR, Ticketmaster (the hold-then-pay flow, with a visible countdown), airline seat selection, IRCTC Tatkal. Ticketmaster adds a virtual waiting room to cap concurrency before the seat map.

Everyday analogy. A restaurant host puts a "reserved" card on a table while you finish ordering; if you do not sit down in 5 minutes the card is removed.

Common interview traps.

  • Check-then-act without a lock: "if seat is free, then book" lets two users both pass the check.
  • Forgetting that payment takes time, so you need a temporary hold, not an immediate booking.
  • Holding seats forever if the user closes the tab (needs expiry).

notes.title: Core entities
notes.html:
• Show: the screening (movie, screen, time, price). Owns its seat states. This is the unit of locking.
  • SeatState: AVAILABLE, LOCKED, BOOKED.
  • Lock info per seat: owner userId and expiry time.
  • Booking: id, show, user, seats, amount. Created only on confirm.
  • BookingService: API: hold, pay (confirm), cancelHold.
  • (Out of scope here: Movie, Theatre, Screen, Payment, User catalog. They are plain data.)

Decision gravity. Making Show the consistency boundary (all seats of one show behind one lock) is simple and correct, and it is reversible: if a show's lock gets hot, move to per-seat locks. Booking stays a separate object created only after payment, so there are no half-bookings to clean up.

Everyday analogy. Each show is a seating chart on a clipboard; whoever holds the clipboard edits it, one person at a time.

Common interview traps.

  • Modelling the lock as a separate global table without tying it to the show, so it is hard to make atomic.
  • Allowing BOOKED to go back to AVAILABLE without a cancellation flow.

notes.title: Class diagram
notes.html:
+---------------------------+          +---------------------------+
| BookingService            |--many--->| Show                      |
| shows: Map<id, Show>      |          | id, pricePerSeat          |
| hold(show,user,seats)     |          | state: Map<seat,State>    |
| pay(show,user,seats)      |          | lockOwner: Map<seat,user> |
| cancelHold(...)           |          | lockExpiry: Map<seat,ms>  |
+---------------------------+          | clock: LongSupplier       |
                                       | lockSeats(user,seats)     |
 <<enum>> SeatState                    | confirm(id,user,seats)    |
 AVAILABLE | LOCKED | BOOKED          | release(user,seats)       |
                                       +---------------------------+
+---------------------------+                      |
| Booking                   |<---------creates-----+
| id, showId, userId        |
| seats, amount             |
+---------------------------+

How to read it. The clock is injected, so tests can move time forward instead of sleeping 5 minutes. All state-changing methods on Show are synchronized, so each is atomic.

Common interview traps.

  • Using System.currentTimeMillis() directly; expiry becomes untestable.
  • Exposing the seat map as a mutable collection.

notes.title: Key patterns
notes.html:
• Pessimistic lock per show (synchronized): Why: the invariant "no seat is sold twice" spans several seats, so one critical section is the simplest way to be correct. Alternative: optimistic version number on the show/seat row and retry on conflict (better when conflicts are rare). Breaks when: one show is so hot that a single lock is the bottleneck. Reversible.
  • Two-phase reservation (hold, then confirm): a classic way to handle slow external steps. The hold is a lease with a TTL, not a permanent claim.
  • Lazy expiry: a lock past its expiry is treated as AVAILABLE the next time anyone looks (expireIfStale). Correctness does not depend on a cleanup thread; a background sweeper is only an optimisation for UI refresh. Why: fewer moving parts, no race between the sweeper and a payment.
  • All-or-nothing: validate every requested seat first, then mutate. No rollback code needed because nothing was changed before validation passed.
  • Strategy (follow-up): pricing (weekday, weekend, premium rows).

Industry examples. Redis SET key value NX PX 300000 is the standard distributed seat-lock primitive (set if absent with a 5-minute expiry); DynamoDB conditional writes or SQL UPDATE seats SET status='LOCKED' WHERE id=? AND status='AVAILABLE' do the same atomically (check rows affected).

Everyday analogy. A library "hold" slip on a book: valid for 3 days, then it goes back to the shelf automatically.

Common interview traps.

  • Confirm without re-validating the lock: payment succeeds at minute 6 after the lock expired and someone else got the seat. Confirm must check "still locked by me".
  • Releasing someone else's lock in cancelHold; check the owner.

notes.title: Code
notes.html:
Full runnable file Main.java (show, atomic lock, confirm, service, test with a 100-thread race):

import java.util.*;
import java.util.concurrent.*;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger;
import java.util.function.LongSupplier;

enum SeatState { AVAILABLE, LOCKED, BOOKED }

class Booking {
    final String id, showId, userId; final List<String> seats; final long amount;
    Booking(String id, String showId, String userId, List<String> seats, long amount) {
        this.id = id; this.showId = showId; this.userId = userId; this.seats = seats; this.amount = amount;
    }
}

/** One screening. ALL seat state for the show lives behind this object's lock, so a multi-seat hold is atomic. */
class Show {
    final String id; final long pricePerSeat;
    private final Map<String, SeatState> state = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    private final Map<String, String> lockOwner = new HashMap<>();
    private final Map<String, Long> lockExpiry = new HashMap<>();
    private final LongSupplier clock; private final long lockTtlMs;

    Show(String id, int rows, int cols, long pricePerSeat, LongSupplier clock, long lockTtlMs) {
        this.id = id; this.pricePerSeat = pricePerSeat; this.clock = clock; this.lockTtlMs = lockTtlMs;
        for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) for (int c = 1; c <= cols; c++) state.put("" + (char) ('A' + r) + c, SeatState.AVAILABLE);
    }

    /** All-or-nothing: either every requested seat is held for this user, or none is. */
    synchronized boolean lockSeats(String userId, List<String> seats) {
        for (String s : seats) {
            if (!state.containsKey(s)) throw new IllegalArgumentException("no seat " + s);
            expireIfStale(s);
            if (state.get(s) != SeatState.AVAILABLE) return false;
        }
        long exp = clock.getAsLong() + lockTtlMs;
        for (String s : seats) { state.put(s, SeatState.LOCKED); lockOwner.put(s, userId); lockExpiry.put(s, exp); }
        return true;
    }

    /** Payment succeeded: lock must still be ours and unexpired, else the seat may already be someone else's. */
    synchronized Booking confirm(String bookingId, String userId, List<String> seats) {
        for (String s : seats) {
            expireIfStale(s);
            if (state.get(s) != SeatState.LOCKED || !userId.equals(lockOwner.get(s)))
                throw new IllegalStateException("lock lost for " + s);
        }
        for (String s : seats) { state.put(s, SeatState.BOOKED); lockOwner.remove(s); lockExpiry.remove(s); }
        return new Booking(bookingId, id, userId, seats, pricePerSeat * seats.size());
    }

    synchronized void release(String userId, List<String> seats) {
        for (String s : seats)
            if (state.get(s) == SeatState.LOCKED && userId.equals(lockOwner.get(s))) free(s);
    }

    synchronized SeatState stateOf(String seat) { expireIfStale(seat); return state.get(seat); }

    private void expireIfStale(String s) {            // lazy expiry: no background thread needed for correctness
        if (state.get(s) == SeatState.LOCKED && clock.getAsLong() >= lockExpiry.get(s)) free(s);
    }
    private void free(String s) { state.put(s, SeatState.AVAILABLE); lockOwner.remove(s); lockExpiry.remove(s); }
}

class BookingService {
    private final Map<String, Show> shows = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final AtomicInteger ids = new AtomicInteger();
    void addShow(Show s) { shows.put(s.id, s); }
    boolean hold(String showId, String userId, List<String> seats) { return shows.get(showId).lockSeats(userId, seats); }
    Booking pay(String showId, String userId, List<String> seats) {
        return shows.get(showId).confirm("BK" + ids.incrementAndGet(), userId, seats);   // payment gateway call would go before this
    }
    void cancelHold(String showId, String userId, List<String> seats) { shows.get(showId).release(userId, seats); }
}

public class Main {
    static void check(boolean c, String msg) { if (!c) throw new AssertionError(msg); }

    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        long[] now = {0};                                   // fake clock
        BookingService svc = new BookingService();
        svc.addShow(new Show("S1", 5, 10, 250, () -> now[0], 5 * 60_000));

        check(svc.hold("S1", "alice", List.of("A1", "A2")), "alice holds");
        check(!svc.hold("S1", "bob", List.of("A2", "A3")), "bob blocked, and A3 must stay free (atomic)");
        check(svc.hold("S1", "bob", List.of("A3")), "A3 was not leaked by the failed attempt");
        Booking b = svc.pay("S1", "alice", List.of("A1", "A2"));
        check(b.amount == 500, "price");

        svc.hold("S1", "bob", List.of("B1"));
        now[0] += 5 * 60_000;                               // lock expires
        check(svc.hold("S1", "carol", List.of("B1")), "carol takes expired seat");
        boolean lost = false;
        try { svc.pay("S1", "bob", List.of("B1")); } catch (IllegalStateException e) { lost = true; }
        check(lost, "bob's late payment rejected");

        // race: 100 users fight for the same seat, exactly one wins
        AtomicInteger winners = new AtomicInteger();
        ExecutorService pool = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(16);
        CountDownLatch go = new CountDownLatch(1), done = new CountDownLatch(100);
        for (int i = 0; i < 100; i++) {
            final String u = "u" + i;
            pool.submit(() -> {
                try { go.await(); if (svc.hold("S1", u, List.of("E5"))) winners.incrementAndGet(); }
                catch (InterruptedException ignored) {} finally { done.countDown(); }
            });
        }
        go.countDown(); done.await(); pool.shutdown();
        check(winners.get() == 1, "exactly one winner, got " + winners.get());
        System.out.println("P10 OK");
    }
}

The core in Kotlin:

enum class SeatState { AVAILABLE, LOCKED, BOOKED }

class Show(val id: String, rows: Int, cols: Int, val price: Long,
           private val clock: () -> Long, private val ttlMs: Long) {
    private val state = LinkedHashMap<String, SeatState>()
    private val owner = HashMap<String, String>()
    private val expiry = HashMap<String, Long>()

    init { for (r in 0 until rows) for (c in 1..cols) state["${'A' + r}$c"] = SeatState.AVAILABLE }

    @Synchronized fun lockSeats(user: String, seats: List<String>): Boolean {
        seats.forEach { require(it in state) { "no seat $it" }; expireIfStale(it) }
        if (seats.any { state[it] != SeatState.AVAILABLE }) return false
        val exp = clock() + ttlMs
        seats.forEach { state[it] = SeatState.LOCKED; owner[it] = user; expiry[it] = exp }
        return true
    }

    @Synchronized fun confirm(user: String, seats: List<String>): Long {
        seats.forEach { expireIfStale(it) }
        check(seats.all { state[it] == SeatState.LOCKED && owner[it] == user }) { "lock lost" }
        seats.forEach { state[it] = SeatState.BOOKED; owner.remove(it); expiry.remove(it) }
        return price * seats.size
    }

    private fun expireIfStale(s: String) {
        if (state[s] == SeatState.LOCKED && clock() >= expiry.getValue(s)) {
            state[s] = SeatState.AVAILABLE; owner.remove(s); expiry.remove(s)
        }
    }
}

Walk-through. lockSeats(bob, [A2, A3]) while Alice holds A2: loop finds A2 is LOCKED, returns false before any write, so A3 is unchanged. confirm at minute 6: expireIfStale frees the seat, the owner check fails, IllegalStateException("lock lost"): the app should now refund the payment (see Concurrency).

Common interview traps.

  • Validating seats and mutating inside the same loop (partial lock on failure).
  • Treating > instead of >= for expiry, creating a one-millisecond window where two people own a seat.

notes.title: Run and test
notes.html:
javac Main.java && java -ea Main
# prints: P10 OK

The test uses a fake clock array. It asserts: Alice's hold works; Bob's overlapping request fails and A3 is not leaked; Alice's payment books both seats at 2 x 250 = 500; a hold expires after exactly 5 minutes and another user can take the seat; Bob's late payment is rejected; and 100 threads released together by a CountDownLatch all try the same seat: exactly one wins.

Common interview traps.

  • A race test that starts threads one by one never really races them. Use a latch.
  • Asserting only "no exception"; assert the number of winners.

notes.title: Concurrency
notes.html:
This is the heart of the problem: the double-booking race. Two requests read "A5 is free" at the same instant, both write "A5 is mine". The fix is making check-and-set atomic.

Options, in the order you would reach for them:

  1. synchronized per show (shown). One JVM, simple, correct. 100 racing threads produce exactly one winner. Throughput is fine: the critical section is a few map operations (microseconds), so one show can serve tens of thousands of holds per second.
  2. Per-seat ReentrantLocks acquired in sorted order (A1 before A2) to avoid deadlock when two users request overlapping seats in different orders. More parallelism, more complexity.
  3. Database atomic update: UPDATE seat SET status='LOCKED', owner=?, expires_at=now()+interval '5 min' WHERE show_id=? AND seat_id IN (...) AND (status='AVAILABLE' OR expires_at<now()); if rows affected differs from the number of seats, roll back. Works across many app servers with no extra infrastructure; the DB row lock is the arbiter.
  4. Redis SET NX PX per seat, with a Lua script to lock multiple seats atomically; a unique constraint in the DB on (show_id, seat_id) in the final bookings table as the last safety net.
  5. Optimistic concurrency: read with a version, write WHERE version = ?, retry on failure. Cheap when conflicts are rare, wasteful on a hot show.

Payment edge case (money and seats must agree). Pay succeeds but confirm fails because the lock expired: you must refund or re-offer. Mitigate by confirming only if at least 30 s of lock remain before starting payment, extending TTL when the gateway call starts, and reconciling with gateway webhooks (idempotent confirm on paymentId).

Incident pattern. Ticket drop for a popular film: 200k users in a minute. Symptom: DB CPU at 100% on the seats table, lock wait timeouts. Fixes: a queue or waiting room to admit users gradually, Redis in front for holds, short transactions, read the seat map from a cache (accept slightly stale display; the hold call is the truth).

Decision gravity. Choosing the database unique constraint (show_id, seat_id) as the final guard is a cheap safety net you should always have, whichever locking you choose.

Everyday analogy. Two people grabbing the last seat at a cinema counter: a single clerk (the lock) serves one at a time, and the second hears "sorry, sold".

Common interview traps.

  • Locking seats one by one without ordering: user X locks A1 then wants A2; user Y locks A2 then wants A1; deadlock.
  • Relying on UI to prevent double booking.
  • Cleaning expired locks only with a cron: seats remain unavailable up to a minute after expiry. Combine lazy expiry with a sweeper.

notes.title: Follow-ups
notes.html:
• Cancellation and refunds: BOOKED to AVAILABLE with a refund policy (time before show).
  • Dynamic pricing / coupons: Strategy on price.
  • Seat-map view: read-through cache, push updates over WebSocket or SSE so other users see seats turn grey.
  • Best-available selection: algorithm picks N adjacent seats in a row.
  • Multiple theatres and cities: shard by city or theatre; each show lives on one shard.
  • Waiting room and bot protection: rate limit by user and IP, reuse the Rate limiter (P11).
  • Notifications: ticket by email/SMS/push, reuse P8.

Common interview traps.

  • Overbooking on purpose (airlines do this) without being asked; confirm business rules first.
  • Not mentioning idempotent payment callbacks.

notes.title: Summary
notes.html:
• The core bug to prevent is check-then-act on a seat; make multi-seat hold atomic (all or nothing).
  • Hold is a lease with TTL; confirm re-checks "still locked by me" because payment is slow.
  • Lazy expiry keeps correctness independent of cleanup threads; inject a clock for tests.
  • Scale-out: DB conditional update or Redis SET NX PX for locks, plus a unique constraint (show, seat) as the final guard.
  • Order lock acquisition to avoid deadlocks; handle "paid but lost the lock" with refund and idempotent webhooks.
